basis: CSX’s April 16, 2025 release establishes that consolidated GAAP revenue for Q1 2025 was $3,423,000,000, down $258,000,000 from $3,681,000,000 in Q1 2024 and below the $3,496,950,000 threshold. April 16 is the earliest qualifying communication I could verify. The earliest public date remains unresolved because I could verify only the opening portion of management’s February 19 Barclays conference remarks.

coverage.detail: October 16, 2024, Q3 earnings cycle. CSX expected a moderate Q4 2024 revenue decline and estimated about $200 million of pressure from fuel prices and coal markets. The forecast applied to the quarter ending December 2024.
November 7 Investor Day. The revenue target was mid-single-digit compound annual growth from 2024 to 2027. It supplied no Q1 2025 revenue bound.
January 23, 2025, previous earnings release. CSX reported $3.54 billion of Q4 2024 revenue, down 4% year over year. The release gave no numeric Q1 2025 consolidated revenue forecast.

January 23 earnings presentation, slide 18. Low- to mid-single-digit growth applied to full-year volume. CSX expected coal prices, diesel prices and traffic mix to weigh on full-year revenue, particularly in the first half.

January 23 call transcript. Management’s roughly 3% sequential Q1 decline forecast applied to coal revenue per unit. The $350 million discussed in Q&A combined earnings pressures, including disruption costs. Neither figure bounded consolidated Q1 revenue.
January 27 Form 8-K exhibit announced Ann Begeman’s board appointment and contained no quarterly sales update.
CSX’s February 11 notice announced a live February 19 webcast with CEO Joe Hinrichs and CFO Sean Pelkey. The notice gives the speakers and time but contains no financial outlook.

The accessible February 19 transcript confirms both executives participated. It ends during the opening audience poll. I could not verify the subsequent Q&A or exclude a quarter-specific forecast there.
March 7 Form 8-K disclosed an underwriting agreement for $600 million of notes due 2035.
March 10 Form 8-K confirmed that the note offering closed. The $600 million was debt principal.

March 11 J.P. Morgan conference. CSX compared January and February daily freight volumes with Q4 daily averages and discussed tunnel disruption. These measures give no year-over-year consolidated revenue bound.

In the March 11 Q&A, Pelkey described Q1 as the expected earnings trough, reported a slower start for volumes and retained full-year volume guidance. He included roughly $10 million per month of disruption costs in the $350 million headwind discussion.
March 19 notice scheduled Q1 results for after market close April 16. It gave no preliminary revenue figure.

April 16 Form 8-K Exhibit 99.2. The consolidated income statement shows revenue of $3,423 million and $3,681 million for the quarters ended March 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Both figures come from the same comparative GAAP table.

publication_date_evidence: CSX’s results release is datelined April 16, 2025. EDGAR accepted the Form 8-K containing the release and comparative financial statements that day at 16:01:28. This verifies public availability of the actuals. [SEC filing index](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000027794825000027/0000277948-25-000027-index.htm)
